subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and what defaults and protected-path behavior should be part of the core backup CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is clear in current source, but defaults and protected paths decide the balance between smaller backups, sensitive-file avoidance, and restorable archives.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle flags, defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, and proof before landing or narrowing it.

options.title: Ship explicit excludes first
options.body: Accept repeatable `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` while deferring smart defaults and automatic ignore-file loading until restore completeness and security expectations are clearer.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Keep core backups coarse for now, document current scope limits, and revisit native filtering only after maintainers decide the recovery and security contract.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle flags, defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, and proof before landing or narrowing it.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and reviewed the original backup CLI contract, so they are the best available owner for the core backup behavior decision.
